skill.name: hig-components-controls

skill.summary: Choose Apple-style input and selection controls with state, validation, and accessibility guidance.

content.value_statement: Choosing the wrong input control can make Apple app workflows confusing. This skill maps common data-entry needs to Apple HIG control guidance.
actual_capabilities: Recommends controls for boolean, numeric, text, and choice-based input needs.
Compares toggles, segmented controls, pickers, sliders, steppers, combo boxes, and token fields.
Explains when control changes should apply immediately or wait for confirmation.
Summarizes platform guidance for iOS, iPadOS, macOS, tvOS, visionOS, and watchOS.
Provides accessibility guidance for labels, current state, VoiceOver, and keyboard behavior.
limitations: It is a guidance reference, not a complete design system or component library.
It does not generate production SwiftUI, UIKit, or AppKit code by itself.
It relies on included reference notes that may not reflect later Apple documentation updates.
It focuses on controls and does not cover navigation, layout, or branding in depth.

use_cases.title: Select Controls For Settings
use_cases.description: Choose toggles, checkboxes, sliders, or steppers based on state, range, and immediacy requirements.

use_cases.title: Review Form Interaction Patterns
use_cases.description: Check whether text fields, pickers, labels, and validation behavior match Apple platform expectations.

use_cases.title: Document Control Usage Rules
use_cases.description: Create consistent guidance for option counts, state display, validation timing, and platform limits.

prompt_templates.title: Pick A Control
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to recommend the best Apple HIG control for a boolean setting that turns sync on or off. Include alternatives to avoid.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Input Options
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to compare a picker, segmented control, and pop-up button for choosing one of twelve categories on iOS.

prompt_templates.title: Review A Form
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review a profile form with text fields, a date picker, a toggle, and validation messages. Identify HIG issues.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Platform Behavior
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to propose control choices for iOS, macOS, and watchOS settings. Explain state, accessibility, validation, and platform differences.

output_examples.input: I need a control for turning notifications on or off in settings.
output_examples.output: Use a switch toggle. It shows a binary state clearly, applies immediately in settings, and needs a clear nearby label.

output_examples.input: I have eight sort choices in an iOS view.
output_examples.output: Avoid a segmented control. Use a picker or menu because eight options make segments hard to scan and tap.

output_examples.input: The user must enter a price between 1 and 100.
output_examples.output: Use a text field when exact entry matters. Add a numeric keyboard, validation, and optional stepper for repeated adjustment.

best_practices: State the data type, option count, platform, and workflow before asking for a control recommendation.
Ask for alternatives when a familiar control may not fit the option count or interaction model.
Include accessibility requirements, validation timing, and state behavior in each design request.
anti_patterns: Do not ask it to choose controls without explaining the data, platform, and number of options.
Do not use segmented controls for long lists or unrelated destinations.
Do not treat gauges or rating indicators as input controls unless the design uses interactive variants.

faq.question: What controls does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers pickers, toggles, sliders, steppers, segmented controls, text inputs, combo boxes, token fields, gauges, and rating indicators.

faq.question: Does it write UI code?
faq.answer: No. It provides control recommendations and design guidance that can inform implementation.

faq.question: Can it help with accessibility?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers labels, VoiceOver context, state clarity, keyboard behavior, and validation communication.

faq.question: Which platforms does it reference?
faq.answer: It references iOS, iPadOS, macOS, tvOS, visionOS, and watchOS guidance where available.

faq.question: How should I phrase requests?
faq.answer: Describe the data type, option count, platform, current control, and when changes should apply.

faq.question: Does it replace Apple documentation?
faq.answer: No. It summarizes bundled references, so check current Apple documentation for recent changes.
